segments: the Turks.
And then there was peace,
and Saladin departed.
And Qilij Arslan returned to Melitene,
and he renewed both of its walls.
And at this time, the Prince of Antioch abandoned his lawful Greek wife, whom he had taken from Constantinople in the days of King Manuel,
and he attached himself to a harlot.
And the Patriarch of Antioch excommunicated the priest who blessed him with the harlot,
and also the whole city,
and he silenced the bells and the prayers.
The Prince, however, was enraged,
and he plundered all the churches and monasteries of the Franks.
Then the Patriarch of Jerusalem came with the counts,
and they reconciled the Prince.
They validated for him that unlawful woman,
and he returned everything that he had seized from the churches and monasteries.
And in that same year died Sayf al-Din Ghazi, son of Qutb al-Din Mawdud, son of Zengi, the lord of Mosul.
And he was a man fond of pleasures,
and constant in the drinking of wine.
And the people of Mosul lived in profound peace and great tranquility during his days.
And there arose in his place as ruler over Mosul,
'Izz al-Din Mas'ud, his brother,
and he was called Abu'l-Fath,
and he conducted himself prudently in all governance.
And Saladin went to Damascus,
and from there he entered Egypt,
and the construction of the citadel of Cairo was completed.
And his brother Shams al-Dawlah died in Alexandria.
And in the year 577,
577 of the Arabs [AH],
al-Malik al-Salih Isma'il, son of Nur al-Din, son of Zengi, the lord of Aleppo, fell sick with a mortal illness.
And when he perceived that he was dying,
he sent to his cousin 'Izz al-Din Mas'ud, the lord of Mosul,
and urged him to come in haste,
so that Aleppo might be handed over [to him],
and Saladin would not take it.
And he also gathered the grandees,
and made them swear an oath on behalf of his cousin; and he died.
It is said
that one of the slaves gave him poison to drink in a cluster of grapes.
Others, however, say
no,
but that he died of the disease of colic.
And the people of Aleppo mourned greatly over him,
because he was splendid in bodily beauty,
and preeminent in spiritual qualities.
And when he died,
dissension fell {among...} {OCR?}
